paragraphs: Overall credibility for this report is unknown, so the results below are for reference only and should not be read as trustworthy or converged. The static step s1 is also unknown. The reaction balance check passed, meaning the applied load and the support reactions cancel.

The mesh quality check is unknown. Second-order elements on curved surfaces became too distorted when upgraded, so straight-edge second-order elements were used and the curved surfaces are approximated by chords. Stress near curved surfaces may therefore deviate noticeably.

In the static step, the maximum von Mises stress away from the constrained faces is {{s1.vm_max_mpa}} and the maximum displacement is {{s1.u_max_mm}}, against a material yield strength of {{s1.strength_mpa}}. Maximum stress over the three mesh levels is {{s1.conv2.level0}}, {{s1.conv2.level1}} and {{s1.conv2.level2}}. Maximum displacement over the same levels is {{s1.conv3.level0}}, {{s1.conv3.level1}} and {{s1.conv3.level2}}. Both mesh-convergence checks passed, but this does not remove the uncertainty from the mesh quality check. No safety factor is given because the credibility checks did not pass (conclusion: unknown).

In the modal step m1, the natural frequencies are {{m1.f1_hz}} ({{m1.f1_rpm}}), {{m1.f2_hz}} ({{m1.f2_rpm}}), {{m1.f3_hz}} ({{m1.f3_rpm}}) and {{m1.f4_hz}} ({{m1.f4_rpm}}). The supports are ideal constraints, so real bearing stiffness would lower these frequencies. Only the part's own mass and stiffness are included, so any attached mass is not represented.

Limitations: the model is linear elastic with small deformation, with no contact, residual stress or surface hardening. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions and were excluded from the maximum stress. Stress at sharp corners grows with mesh refinement (a theoretical singularity) and should not be used directly as a design basis.
suggestions: Reduce the element size on the curved surfaces so that there are at least a few element layers across them, then rerun so that second-order elements can be upgraded without excessive distortion.
Recheck the stress near the curved surfaces after remeshing, because the current chord approximation may bias it.
Have an engineer review the sharp corners in the model and decide whether to add fillets or use a hot-spot or notch-stress method instead of the raw peak stress.
Provide the actual bearing stiffness and replace the ideal supports in the modal model to obtain more realistic frequencies.
Provide the attached masses and add them to the modal model before comparing frequencies with operating speeds.
